ut_spirit_walker_cave.blurb: Spirit Walker Cave is a steep, shady cave tucked into the talus of the Upper Boulder Field above Ogden, in the northern Wasatch. It holds ten boulder problems on quartzite, and it is the place around Ogden where the hardest bouldering is concentrated. The spread is lopsided: a couple of V5s at the bottom end, a cluster of V10 and V11 lines in the middle, and a few problems at the very top of the scale that reach into the V13 to V14 range. It is not a spot for warming up or for beginners. Because the cave stays out of the sun, it can be considered even in warmer weather once you have made it up the scramble.

ut_book_of_condolences.blurb: Book of Condolences is a bolted wall in the Red Corners section of American Fork Canyon, in the southern Wasatch. The cliff folds back on itself like an accordion, and this stretch in the middle has the densest cluster of lines and the busiest routes of the whole section. All ten climbs are sport routes, and they are firmly for experienced climbers: two at 5.11, most at 5.12 and 5.13, and one 5.14. Expect technical, sustained climbing, including a hard open corner that rewards stemming and precise footwork. Cooler temperatures help on the greasier lines, so fall or an early start in summer suits it best.

ut_hidden_boulder.blurb: Hidden Boulder is a single compact boulder, roughly ten feet tall, tucked among the other blocks of the Lower Boulder Field in Ogden's quartzite bouldering zone. Despite its name it sits right in the main part of the field, toward the southern side. Its ten problems are mostly easy to moderate, running from V0 up to a V5 at the hard end, with plenty of short, fun lines covering the faces and a roof. The main face and the roof look north. That makes it a handy stop for warming up, for newer boulderers, or for anyone wanting several low-stress problems on one rock.

ut_sumo_wall_the.blurb: The Sumo Wall is a sport crag in the Welcome Springs area, west of St. George in southwest Utah's desert hills. It has ten bolted routes with a good spread: one easy 5.6, a few mid-grade lines around 5.8 and 5.9, then three each at 5.10 and 5.11 and one 5.12. That mix makes it friendly for climbers working up through the moderates as well as those looking for something harder. The wall catches the sun until early afternoon and has a shorter walk than the neighbouring Cathedral wall, so it can work as a lower-effort day among the Welcome Springs crags.
ut_sumo_wall_the.approach: From the wooden corrals, follow the wash past the cottonwoods. The wall is the first prominent one on your left; the trail up to it is partly hidden behind a large boulder.

ut_sun_king_east_face.blurb: Sun King, East Face is a sport wall on the Sun King dome in the Devil's Playground area of Utah's West Desert. It holds ten bolted routes that stay on the friendly side: four around 5.6, a few at 5.8 and 5.9, and two at 5.10, so it suits newer leaders and anyone after a relaxed day. The face picks up the early sun and goes shady later in the day, which makes it a good morning stop. The dome has climbing on its other side as well, and a lower outcropping nearby has short top-rope climbs.

ut_cobble_roof.blurb: The Cobble Roof is one of the signature walls of Box Canyon in Maple Canyon, central Utah. It is a big curved roof on the east side of the corridor, just where the canyon bends right shortly after you enter the box. All ten routes are sport climbs, and the wall is hard: most are 5.13, with a 5.12 and a 5.10 beside them, and just a couple of easier 5.6 and 5.7 lines at the other end. Expect steep, powerful climbing on cobbles. The shade makes it a good choice for escaping the summer sun.

ut_shady_acres_main_wall.blurb: Shady Acres Main Wall is the principal wall in a narrow side canyon off the Maple Canyon road in central Utah. Its ten sport routes are all in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a few at 5.10 and most at 5.11. Routes tend to start with a bouldery move or two, ease into gently overhanging or vertical ground, and finish steeper on the longer lines. The wall is in shade until early afternoon and the canyon floor stays shaded all day, so it suits warm days. A stick clip and a 70 metre rope are useful for some lines, and a helmet is wise for the belayer.
ut_shady_acres_main_wall.approach: Starting near the Bumper Wall, walk to the Eco-Terrorist wall and follow it down canyon through a small notch. The side canyon and the main wall are then on your right.

ut_roadside_crag.blurb: Roadside Crag is a short bolted wall in Echo Canyon, in the Wasatch Back, sitting right beside the frontage road north of I-80, about three miles from the exit. The wall is roughly 35 to 50 feet tall, and there is essentially no walk, so it is quick to get to and suits an after-work session. All ten routes are sport climbs on the easier side: mostly 5.9 and 5.10 with a couple of 5.7 and 5.8 lines below them. The routes are well bolted, which makes it a comfortable choice for newer leaders. Room to park is limited.
